  equal shares. AIMD is both
  a stability mechanism and a
   fairness mechanism, which
  is why every later design
  still ends with a
  multiplicative backoff.

  Reno's weakness was
  multiple losses. One
  retransmission per RTT,
  with duplicate-ACK counters
   that stall after two
  losses in a window, sent
  many connections into
  timeouts and slow-start
  restarts. NewReno (1996)
  patched this within the
  vanilla ACK stream,
  retransmitting through
  several losses per window.
  SACK (RFC 2018) solved it
  with information instead of
   guessing: the receiver
  lists the out-of-order
  blocks it holds, and the
  sender repairs precisely,
  with FACK and later RACK
  sharpening the
  loss-detection logic.

  By the late nineties a
  deeper limitation appeared.
   AIMD's halve-and-climb
  response
